🔥🇲🇽 <u>INE'S OWN WATCHDOG HAS 18 OPEN CASES</u>

The INE's Internal Control Office has 18 open investigations into the institute's own officials: 5 already escalated to serious-misconduct proceedings and 13 still under investigation. They cover conflicts of interest, concealed information, irregular contracting and misuse of public funds. Controller Víctor Hugo Carvente says the headlines were no surprise: "We had already identified these facts in the audit area." The biggest winner of the electoral-materials oligopoly is Cajas Graf, with 1,072.9 million pesos in contracts since 2014.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>GHOST WORKERS AND PURGES IN TADDEI'S INE</u>

Former INE staff describe Guadalupe Taddei's circle running the institute as a patronage machine, with "aviadores" on the payroll who only showed up months later to sign their resignations and collect severance. In the Gender and Non-Discrimination unit, Taddei's appointee Iliana Araceli Hernández Gómez swept out all 12 structural staff and 24 contract workers. She also pressured an administrative liaison to quit while on ISSSTE-certified leave for a high-risk pregnancy. The complaints are now before the INE's Internal Control Office and the Electoral Tribunal.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>VULCAN'S CALICA HEADS FOR ANOTHER SUPREME COURT LOSS</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court is set to throw out Calica's amparo against the 2022 suspension of its customs permit at Punta Venado, Quintana Roo, which keeps its limestone export halt in place. Justice Loretta Ortiz Ahlf flagged grounds to dismiss the case without even reaching the merits and gave the Vulcan Materials subsidiary three business days to argue otherwise. The fight began on May 10, 2022, when customs agency ANAM suspended the permit for breached conditions. A Cancún federal judge already upheld that suspension in 2023.

🇲🇽🏗️ <u>Infrastructure spending up 60.5% in September, the biggest jump since 2013</u>

Mexico's infrastructure spending rose 60.5% year on year in September, the biggest increase for that month since 2013, Hacienda data reported by El Economista show. Public investment through the third quarter reached 637,631 million pesos, up 8%. Education infrastructure grew 316% and health 228%. "The Mexican economy extended its recovery during the third quarter, supported by stronger public and private investment," said Finance Secretary Édgar Amador.

🇲🇽🚔 <u>Baja California now pays its police the most in Mexico</u>

In her fifth report, Governor Marina del Pilar said Baja California ranks first nationally in police pay, with an average of 25,967 pesos a month. The state set up a 1.5 billion-peso trust fund for 2023-2027 to fund benefits and social security for more than 2,300 members of its security and prison forces. Every state force officer gets a 5,000-peso annual bonus, and cadet stipends have doubled to 12,000 pesos a month.

🇲🇽📉 <u>State debt falls: 13 billion pesos less in a year</u>

According to the Auditoría Superior de la Federación, debt owed by Mexico's states and Mexico City fell to 717,898.6 million pesos in 2025, down from 731 billion in 2024. That's a drop of 13,103.7 million pesos. The burden is still concentrated: five states hold 54% of it, 324,702 million pesos. The ASF also warned that states still rely on short-term loans to cover liquidity gaps, an area the law has yet to define clearly.

🇲🇽💰 <u>Mexico paid 159 billion pesos less in debt interest than budgeted</u>

Through September, interest on Mexico's public debt came in 159,350.8 million pesos below the budget, according to Hacienda. The reasons: a stronger peso, better interest rates and refinancing operations. Interest payments also fell 3.7% in real terms compared with January to September 2025. Hacienda and private analysts say those savings largely explain how the deficit is being kept in check.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex fuel-theft losses drop 26.6% in Q3</u>

According to annexes to Pemex's third-quarter report reviewed by El Economista, fuel theft cost the company 18,218 million pesos from January to September 2026. That's 10% below the 20,246 million lost in the same period of 2025. For July through September alone, losses fell to 5,226 million pesos from 7,125 million a year earlier, a 26.6% drop.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>6,338 million pesos in scholarships for Guanajuato</u>

Sheinbaum announced 6,338 million pesos in Becas para el Bienestar for Guanajuato: 502,161 primary students, 264,626 in secondary school and 189,502 in high school. That's more than 950,000 young people in a state the PAN has governed since 1991. She also confirmed a new Universidad Rosario Castellanos campus in Celaya.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>Trains and housing are moving nearly 1% of Mexico's GDP</u>

While inspecting the Querétaro–Irapuato line (25% complete, serving 2 million people), Sheinbaum said passenger rail and Vivienda para el Bienestar are the public works doing the most to drive the economy, contributing close to 1% of GDP this year. Mexico is building about 2,500 km of track: roughly 300 km for freight, the rest for intercity and metropolitan passenger service. INEGI's flash estimate put third-quarter growth at 3.2% year on year, the strongest since 2023.
